title: Ram Asrey v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sanjay Misra and Anant Kumar, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; Clause 6.5 application to be decided in accordance with law
headnote: A pending application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is to be considered and decided by the competent authority in accordance with law and within the time stipulated in that clause. The High Court will not examine the consumer's billing claim on merits in a writ seeking to stall recovery and to have the application decided.
facts: Ram Asrey sought a mandamus restraining recovery of electricity dues and directing decision of his application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He had earlier sued the Power Corporation for injunction; the suit and the subsequent appeal were both dismissed. He then applied to the Corporation on 21 June 2013 under Clause 6.5. That application remained pending. Corporation counsel submitted that if the petitioner fulfilled the clause's conditions, the competent authority would decide it.

holding_units.holding: Where a consumer's application under Clause 6.5 remains pending before the competent authority, a writ seeking to restrain recovery of dues and to have that application decided will be disposed of by leaving it to that authority to consider and decide the application in accordance with law, within the time stipulated in Clause 6.5, without the Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the claim.

not_decided.point: Merits of the petitioner's Clause 6.5 billing claim and the prayer to restrain recovery of dues
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits, which were left to the competent authority under Clause 6.5.
